title: Maximum Number of Upgradable Servers
summary: Given n data centers, you are provided with four arrays: count, upgrade, sell, and money.
statement: Given n data centers, you are provided with four arrays: count, upgrade, sell, and money. The array count indicates the number of servers in each data center, upgrade shows the cost to upgrade a single server, sell provides the money received from selling a server, and money gives the initial amount of money for each data center. For each data center, determine the maximum number of servers that can be upgraded, ensuring that the money from one data center cannot be used to upgrade servers in another data center. Return an array where each element corresponds to the maximum number of servers that can be upgraded in the respective data center.
constraints: All four arrays have the same nonzero length; costs and sale prices are positive and counts and money are nonnegative.
Within each data center, sell any non-upgraded servers and use its starting money to upgrade the rest.
Return the maximum number upgraded independently for every center.
reference_solution:
def maximum_upgradable_servers(count,upgrade,sell,money):
    return [min(size,(cash+size*sale)//(cost+sale)) for size,cost,sale,cash in zip(count,upgrade,sell,money)]
hints: If x servers are upgraded, the other count-x may be sold, so affordability is x*upgrade≤money+(count-x)*sell.
Rearrange the inequality to isolate x and cap the quotient by count.
The affordability inequality is monotone in x; its largest integral solution is exactly the capped quotient.
editorial: The affordability inequality is monotone in x; its largest integral solution is exactly the capped quotient.

tests.explanation: The centers can afford three and two upgrades respectively after selling the unused servers.
Selling one server yields only one unit, so no server can be upgraded.
